statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2018-15919 lets a remote client find out whether an account exists when sshd accepts GSSAPI authentication: in userauth_gssapi() in auth2-gss.c, a failed GSSAPI context setup for an existing account sets a server-caused-failure flag, so the attempt does not count against MaxAuthTries, while an attempt for an unknown account counts and the server disconnects after MaxAuthTries attempts (https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2018/08/27/2, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-15919, https://bugs.debian.org/907503). The OpenSSH developers do not treat account-existence oracles of this kind as significant vulnerabilities (https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2018/08/24/1). No OpenSSH release changes this code, and the Debian security tracker lists every Debian release, including trixie, as vulnerable and rates it unimportant. OpenSSH 10.0p1 and Debian's patched source keep the same logic in userauth_gssapi(). The DHI Debian repository publishes three builds of openssh for Debian 13, all rebuilds of Debian's 1:10.0p1-7+deb13u4. We checked the openssh-server and openssh-client packages and their debug-symbol packages for all three builds on amd64 and arm64, each verified against the index checksum, and the source of Debian's 1:10.0p1-7+deb13u4 (https://salsa.debian.org/ssh-team/openssh/-/tree/debian/1%2510.0p1-7+deb13u4). In every build, sshd-auth, the program that runs user authentication, links libgssapi_krb5.so.2 and its debug symbols contain userauth_gssapi. This owner carries no change to this code, so every published build is affected. The behaviour can only be reached when GSSAPIAuthentication is set to yes; it defaults to no, and the shipped sshd_config leaves it at the default.
